mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order of X and Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions 'the difference between ... and ...' or a similar phrase indicating a signed difference.
mathgap.example: Treating 'the difference between A and B' as |A - B| (absolute value) instead of A - B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), preserving the direction of the comparison.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says one person has N more or fewer items than another.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has N more than B' as A = N, ignoring B's count.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A's current count to N at that moment, overriding any previous value for A.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement gives an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Keeping an earlier count for A unchanged after a later statement 'A has N items'.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in the order given; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements, using the updated counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains both transfer statements and relational statements.
mathgap.example: Evaluating a relational equation using counts before a preceding transfer has been applied.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of each pair.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X that Y has more than Z is equal to the difference between the number of A and B'.
mathgap.example: Translating such a statement as X = A - B, dropping the '- Z' part.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by a numeric operation other than direct assignment or transfer (e.g., multiplication, subtraction), apply that operation to the current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says a person's count 'increases by X times', 'decreases by X', or similar.
mathgap.example: Treating 'increase by 3 times' as adding 3 instead of multiplying by 3.

mathgap.title: Split All Items Equally Among Recipients
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two or more recipients, set each recipient's count to the total divided by the number of recipients.
mathgap.example: Assigning each recipient the whole amount instead of dividing it equally.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two or more persons redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount, set each person's count to the average of their combined items.
mathgap.example: Setting each person's count to the sum of all items instead of the average.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Collect all statements that involve any variable, not only those that mention the queried person, to capture indirect constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, gather every constraint from the problem before attempting to solve.
mathgap.example: Ignoring statements that do not mention the target variable, missing constraints that affect it.

mathgap.title: Interpret 'increase by N times' as multiplication
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a quantity 'increases by X times', treat it as multiplying the current count by X.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering phrasing like 'increase by N times' or 'multiply by N'.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often defaults to thinking of 'difference' as magnitude, ignoring the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always interpret 'difference between X and Y' as X - Y, preserving the order given.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model tends to treat transfers as a separate batch applied after processing all constraints.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears, before evaluating later relational statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts set a permanent baseline, ignoring subsequent give/take actions.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current count at that point, which can be modified by later transfers.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may simplify an equation like (A - B) = (C - D) to A = C, dropping the '- B' and '- D' parts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate difference equalities fully as (A - B) = (C - D) and keep both terms on each side.

mathgap.description: Incomplete processing of problem statements: stopping after a subset of constraints or ignoring many statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model may think it has enough information early and ignore later statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Systematically extract and consider every statement in the problem before solving.
